Lia (Support): FYI customer 'acrobatics.ai' reporting 503s for hosted inference since ~09:02 UTC. They see 'upstream unavailable' and request id 0b3f... attached. Customer says it started after a spike in load. Escalating to eng/sre. :rotating_light:
Sophia (SRE): I see a correlated spike in upstream worker restarts from the metrics. Crash loop on inference-worker pods in us-west-2. Sending kube events and crash logs.
oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-342 (assigned to SRE rota)
Devon (Runtime): Uploading the tail of the worker logs, looks like repeated cuda mem alloc failures then segfaults.
Devon (Runtime): ```
[2026-03-15T09:01:22Z] runtime: allocating kv cache for seq_len=2048 tokens
E 09:01:22 inference-worker-7: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory\E 09:01:22 inference-worker-7: Assertion `0 == cudaSuccess' failed.
SIGSEGV (core dumped)
```
Akshay (ML Infra): Which model and instance type? Could be a batchsize/kv-cache regression or driver mismatch.
Lia (Support): Customer said model 'redwood/open-7b-v1' on hosted, default plan. They didn't change config. They did a traffic spike 1000 req/s.
Sophia (SRE): Node kernel and nvidia-driver versions updated in us-west-2 last week. I'm seeing node oom_killer events and container restarts with exit code 139.
Maya (Customer Success): Customer is on a critical path for demo in 3 hours. What's a safe mitigation?
Sophia (SRE): Short term mitigation: pin requests to fallback smaller model variant and throttle concurrency for their API key. We can also route to dedicated soft-fallback pool (CPU or smaller GPU).
Devon (Runtime): Quick config we can apply: set route policy `max_concurrency: 4` and a `fallback_model: open-3b` for that customer id. Also reduce `max_sequence_length` from 2048 -> 1024 for on-hosted.
Akshay (ML Infra): Suggest enabling aggressive kv-cache eviction for that model and lowering batch size. Also check if quantized variant is available to reduce VRAM.
Sophia (SRE): Repro steps I'm running now: replaying customer's traffic against a staging worker with same node image to reproduce OOM. If we can repro, we'll capture coredump and check stack.
Devon (Runtime): If you get a core, run `eu-stack` and capture `backtrace` from the runtime symbol map. Also check whether the allocator is hitting a fragmentation path: `nvidia-smi dmon` during replay.
Sophia (SRE): I repro'd locally: after sustained 700 req/s with average seq_len ~1200, worker uses >96% GPU mem then coredumps. Looks like cumulative KV cache growth not bounded under certain batching patterns.
Lia (Support): Logging the customer-facing ticket and telling them temporary fallback will be applied. They'll accept reduced perf for now.
Devon (Runtime): Pushing a hotfix to runtime to enforce a hard cap on kv_cache bytes per session and to fail fast with 429 rather than crash. Patch PR: `github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4521`
k8s-deploy-bot: Deployment started for runtime-hf/kv-cap: canary -> 3 pods
Sophia (SRE): Rolling canary applied. Monitoring: memory usage stable on canary pods. No OOMs in the last 6 min.
Akshay (ML Infra): We should also add an autoscaler rule to prefer spinning up additional small-gpu workers instead of packing more sessions per pod during spikes. Filing infra task INFRA-867.
Maya (Customer Success): I'll confirm with customer and keep them updated. Thanks team.
Lia (Support): Post-mortem action items: (1) add kv-cache bounded-limits test in CI, (2) enable customer-specific throttles on hosted plan, (3) backport runtime hard-fail to stable. Assigning owners in the incident ticket.
Sophia (SRE): Adding logs and the coredump analysis to the ticket. Root cause draft: unbounded kv-cache growth + higher-than-expected batch concurrency + recent driver/kernel combo increased effective allocation pressure -> gpu allocation failures -> segfault on assertion.
Devon (Runtime): Long term: add telemetry for per-session kv_cache size, regression test for high-throughput patterns, consider GC of inactive sessions.
Lia (Support): Customer updated: mitigation applied (fallback + throttle). They see fewer 503s. Closing customer escalation; keeping incident open for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
